build: site data 2.1.2.0; offline refit of the 14 to 16 October bullet-hole observations (L4040 to L4047), game not launched
question: Is RecoilDecreaseOffset 0 with a refitted factor scale a better recovery law than the applied x0.8 on the 56 hole observations, and does it hold on weapons left out of the fit?
method: fit-offset.mjs: the scoring, seeds and observations of fit-stretch.mjs (L4049) unchanged; offset swept from 0 to the stored 0.06 with C refitted by golden-section search (200 seeds, final score 500 seeds); leave-one-weapon-out with C fitted on three weapons and scored on the fourth. climb-tables.mjs for the site climb.

control.description: stored law 1099.5 and applied x0.8 359.2, equal to L4049

points: The score falls monotonically as the offset falls; the best value is the boundary 0 (C 0.865, 270.6 against 358.9 at 0.06 with C free).
The gain is in the pair bands (299.5 to 208.9), mostly the AK-205 and TR-7 from 290 to 350 ms; burst extents are unchanged (59.4 to 61.7).
Held-out weapons: offset 0 scores 95.9 / 57.2 / 147.5 / 25.8 (AK-205 / LMR27 / TR-7 / M433) against 119.5 / 56.5 / 180.3 / 28.9 at the stored offset; sum 326.4 against 385.2.
Both laws still miss the 290 to 350 ms bands by half or more (AK-205 Standard 292 ms: observed 0.101, x0.8 0.021, offset 0 0.061) and score about 5 per observation.
Site effect: mean aim before shot 15 falls 3.2 to 6.0 percent on the four weapons.
limits: Offset 0 contradicts the stored 0.06 on every measured weapon; no source mechanism is known.
Four recovery profiles, all with RecoilDecreaseExponent 1; bolt-actions and shotguns (0.6) are untested.
A boundary optimum can mean a missing term rather than a true zero.
